A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCPU research. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 adds readable Appendices 7.1–7.4.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Llama-7B pruning experiments, including perplexity, downstream accuracy, compensation ablations, and resource measurements.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original experiments on Llama-7B, Llama-2-13B, and Vicuna-7B, including additional comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains variance-aware column selection, the Procrustes solution Q = UVᵀ, rotation of retained weights, and optional isotropic scaling. The revised least-squares procedure is a comparison baseline; no operational change to RCPU is established.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText-2 for calibration and perplexity, and BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, and OpenBookQA for downstream evaluation. The additional models are evaluated on these retained tasks; no new dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SliceGPT comparisons on Llama-2-13B (Tables 3 and 7); v1 only discussed SliceGPT. It also replaces the unconstrained output-map LS comparator with Ridge-regularized fitting of retained weights and adds this comparator to downstream accuracy tables, including the retained Llama-7B experiment in Table 2.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from Llama-7B with 128 calibration samples to include Llama-2-13B and Vicuna-7B with 128 and 512 samples. Figure 2 introduces an 8–512-sample sweep. The Ridge comparison searches λ from 10⁻⁶ to 10⁶, selecting by perplexity on the fitting calibration data (Sections 4.2 and 7.1).

E4.justification: v2 adds calibration-size sensitivity analysis (Figure 2) and extensive Ridge regularization sensitivity analyses (Figures 5–6), and expands score-by-compensation comparisons across calibration sizes and models (Figures 3–4). The original projection-target ablation is retained unchanged as Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added calibration sample counts and hyperparameter sweeps do not introduce run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original Llama-7B/128 table results are retained, while v2 adds substantial results for new model, calibration, and comparator settings. New findings distinguish perplexity from downstream accuracy: at 30% pruning on Vicuna-7B with 512 samples, Ridge has lower PPL than rotation-only RCPU (20.52 versus 21.55), but lower mean accuracy (57.32 versus 57.56; Tables 8 and 10).

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces the unconstrained output-map objective and pseudoinverse solution with a regularized retained-weight objective and its closed-form solution. Section 4.2 adds effective-degrees-of-freedom formulas and comparisons. The core Procrustes mathematics remains intact, although Equation 8 changes the scale constraint from s ≥ 0 to s > 0.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain geometry-preserving post-pruning compensation combined with variance-aware scoring, requiring no additional architectural changes and modest computation. The broad claims of better perplexity and task accuracy remain; additional model evaluations provide supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 develops a calibration-dependent interpretation of Ridge compensation: improved perplexity with more samples need not imply better downstream generalization (Sections 4.2 and 7.4). It adds arguments involving effective degrees of freedom and tuning cost, explains scaling benefits through more stable norm estimates, and proposes accumulated distribution mismatch as an explanation for SliceGPT results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link in Section 4.1 and documents the Ridge search grid and calibration-based selection rule. The original projection-pruning details, evaluation harness, and A100 80GB hardware disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds RotPruner and DenoiseRotator and distinguishes their learned pruning-oriented rotations from RCPU's analytic compensation after removal. It also adds references supporting Ridge regression, effective degrees of freedom, and Llama 2. The broader compression literature and positioning relative to FLAP remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The six main sections retain their order and much of their wording. v2 locally revises the least-squares discussion, experimental interpretation, and conclusion, converts some numbered subsections into paragraph headings, and adds an ethics/reproducibility statement and appendix structure. Title, affiliation, and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains model and calibration-size columns, and the original two-panel compensation figure becomes the four-panel Figure 3. v2 adds calibration-size and regularization plots, a second-model comparison figure, and multiple benchmark tables. The original projection-ablation and efficiency tables are retained and renumbered, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation on one model and one calibration budget, and its reliance on an unconstrained LS comparator. Additional models, evaluated SliceGPT and tuned Ridge comparisons, and calibration/regularization sensitivity analyses make the central robustness argument much better supported and its boundaries more visible. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported, and superiority wording remains too broad: Table 7 favors WANDA-sp over both RCPU variants at 10% and 20% pruning. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in empirical support.
